instruction.name: b
instruction.description: Branch unconditionally (target is the next instruction).

throughput.name: 8 taken branches, 40 static sites (fits in the BTB)
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 4 --unroll2 5 --iters 30000 --warmup 10 --reps 9 --core 0 --asm 'b 4; b 4; b 4; b 4; b 4; b 4; b 4; b 4'
throughput.notes: Taken branches to the next instruction, 8 lanes x 4 static sites; the slope method compares 8x4 with 8x5 bodies, so at most 40 branch sites, which fits in the LA464 BTB: 1 cycle per branch.

throughput.name: 8 taken branches, 512 static sites (exceeds the BTB)
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 120 --unroll2 128 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 9 --core 0 --asm 'b 4; b 4; b 4; b 4; b 4; b 4; b 4; b 4'
throughput.notes: Same sequence with 8 lanes x 120 static sites (compared against 8x128, 960-1024 sites), far beyond the LA464 BTB: about 3 cycles per branch. Together with the fits-in-BTB case this brackets the BTB capacity: 40 sites still sustain 1 CPI, 56 sites already degrade to ~3 CPI.

notes: No destination data dependency; latency is not defined. Throughput depends on whether the static branch footprint fits in the BTB: 1 CPI when it fits, ~3 CPI once it overflows. Both cases are recorded.
